power in one persons hands is neither possible nor a option in a democracy ultimately we the people choose the house of representatives hor and then the hor chooses the prime minister the hor has a total of 275 members out of these 165 are directly elected through the first past the post fptp system via election these 165 members are openly and directly elected by the people and you clearly know whom you are voting for essentially they are our voice in parliament since it is not feasible for everyone to go to parliament we elect representatives to speak and act on our behalf the remaining 110 seats are allocated proportionally based on the performance of parties in the fptp elections a party that wins more direct seats gets more proportional seats while a party that wins fewer seats gets fewer proportional seats these seats come from a closed list submitted by political parties making it a party decision so the total comes to 275 seats which form the core of nepals federal parliament its important to understand that the hor is the real center of power in the federal parliament not the prime minister the pm is essentially an initiator or manager but ultimate authority lies with the parliament who passes critical bills and laws bills and laws can be proposed by members of the federal parliament and cabinets but they must be approved by the hor and in some cases also by the national assembly what about constitutional amendments this is what we really need right now right to amend the constitution a twothirds majority is required in both the hor 184275 and the national assembly 4059 and let me quickly tell you even with a twothirds majority the fundamental principles of the constitution cannot be changed for example making murder legal or restricting freedom of speech this is the strength of a federal democratic system so the real question is do we need balen or do we need the right 275 members in the federal parliament of nepal the prime minister whoever they may be is not that much important what matters is having capable and responsible parliamentarians instead of focusing on a single individual our focus should have been finding the 275 people who discussion why some people on the left say liberal democracy and fascism arent fundamentally that different firstly im not a tankie but one claim i often hear in some parts of the left is that liberal democracy and a fascist state arent fundamentally that different i understand why that sounds absurd or confusing at first still at least in this specific regard i think theres a serious argument behind it and id like to try to explain it here for the sake of discussion the point is not that life under fascism and life under liberal democracy feel the same obviously they dont the claim is about the structure not experience historically fascism almost never comes to power by completely dismantling the existing political systems it inherits the same institutions courts police bureaucracy emergency laws prisons the military their members etc in most cases fascists did not even need to write a new constitution or build a new state from scratch they mostly take over what already existed before what really changes is how these tools are used and justified liberal democracies already contain all the same mechanisms of coercion and repression strike breaking surveillance detention without trial emergency powers political policing and so on the fascist state later uses these actions though are framed as exceptional temporary or necessary in moments of crisis and legitimised by the democratic nature of the government but when they happen the concrete results are often indistinguishable from those produced by openly authoritarian systems people get beaten jailed silenced removed from political life etc fascism in contrast does not invent these mechanisms new it just removes the need to pretend they are exceptions another important part of the argument concerns power itself we often say that democracy makes power limited and accountable in contrast to fascist regimes though there were some with elections even but only a very specific and tiny layer of power is
